commit.subject: feat(codex): read Codex sessions straight from rollout files

entries.text: Addition from the coordinator, fold it into your plan: Codex's workspace-write sandbox blocks writes to .git (git commit fails with 'Unable to create .git/index.lock: Operation not permitted'). So in CI the common pattern is: codex exec edits files, then a later workflow step commits. That commit has no 'git commit' action in any session. Support it: a commit with no matching commit action gets the session(s) in that worktree whose last activity ended before the commit time and after the previous commit's time, matched as 'session' (a third match kind, shown in the viewer like the others), whole session segment since the previous commit. Keep sha/time matches preferred. Cover it with a test, and document it in docs/production.md (CI section). Also: the <path> commits are being re-recorded right now; wait until 'git -C <path> log --oneline' shows the wordfreq commits before step 7.

I'm grouping commit 3 around the rollout reader—rolloutThread, CodexRollouts, their fixtures and tests, plus ServerConfig and the related test fakes—while noting Ledger.test's codexHome fake should actually move to commit 4.

Wait, I realize Ledger.test lacks codexHome at commit 3, which would break typecheck there, so I need an intermediate version of Ledger.test with just the codexHome line added after codexBin, keeping ThreadStore.ts empty and CodexSessions.ts's only change being the `disabled` flag.
Commit 3: the rollout reader. The old Ledger test needs the new `codexHome` config field to typecheck at this commit, so I'm staging HEAD's version with just that line added.

entries.title: git commit -q -F - <<EOF 2>&1 · git log --oneline -1 · git status --short
entries.command:
cd . && export PATH=$PWD/node_modules/.bin:$PATH && git -c user.email=<private> commit -q -F - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | grep -v "^\[" ; git log --oneline -1; git status --short
feat(codex): read Codex sessions straight from rollout files

CodexRollouts lists and reads sessions from $CODEX_HOME/sessions without
`codex app-server`, for places with neither T3 nor the app-server (CI after
`codex exec`). core/rolloutThread.ts rebuilds the thread/read result from a
rollout's item_completed events, so both paths give the same entries: a
test pins this on a real `codex exec` session (scrubbed) and the
app-server's answer for it. Unknown lines are skipped, never the session;
history a delegated thread inherited is hidden, as thread/read does.

Checked against `codex app-server` on 195 local sessions: 189 identical,
4 /review subagents (same entries, listed by neither), 2 where the
app-server masks secrets in commands.

Also adds ServerConfig.codexHome (CODEX_HOME), ThreadStore.empty and
CodexSessions.disabled for the ledger's sources.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
